PHARM 2 - week 3 - autonomic drugs + analgesics
** pharm quiz moved to THURS 9am, bring calculator **
zoom link on canvas

Beta blockers (e.g. propranolol, atenolol, metoprolol)
- MOA: block beta-adrenergic receptors -> decrease HR + contractility
- uses: hypertension, angina, post-MI, arrhythmias, anxiety (propranolol)
- SE: bradycardia, fatigue, cold extremities, bronchospasm
- CI: asthma (non-selective ones esp.), heart block
- cardioselective = beta1 selective (atenolol, metoprolol) -> safer in asthma but still caution

ACE inhibitors (-pril e.g. ramipril, lisinopril)
MOA: inhibit angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) -> less angiotensin II -> vasodilation + less aldosterone
SE: dry cough (bradykinin build up!!), hyperkalaemia, angioedema, first dose hypotension
CI pregnancy - teratogenic

Paracetamol
max dose 4g / 24h in adults
overdose -> hepatotoxicity, treat w/ N-acetylcysteine (NAC) ideally within 8 hrs

NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen, aspirin)
- inhibit COX-1 and COX-2 -> less prostaglandins
- SE: GI bleeding/ulcers, renal impairment, asthma exacerbation
aspirin is irreversible COX inhibitor -> antiplatelet effect lasts the life of the platelet (~7-10 days)

Opioids - morphine is the prototype mu receptor agonist
SE: constipation (no tolerance develops!), resp depression, nausea, miosis
naloxone = opioid antagonist used to reverse overdose (short half life so may need repeat doses)

Q for tutor: why does warfarin interact with so many drugs??
